task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 3, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style news update for a general-interest newspaper about Brindle Kiln Glass's furnace conversion and the consequences for workers, customers and the local power system.

facts.text: Brindle Kiln Glass announced on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026, that it will replace the gas furnace at its Dunmere bottle plant with an electric furnace.
The company expects production to stop for six weeks beginning Jan. 11, 2027, while the old furnace is removed.
The announced project budget is $16 million, including a $4 million grant from the fictional Fen County Industrial Fund.
The remaining $12 million will come from company funds and a bank loan; the loan's interest rate was not disclosed.
The plant has 96 production employees, all of whom received written offers for work during the shutdown.
The offers assign 68 employees to training, 16 to maintenance work and 12 to a company plant 34 miles away.
Base hourly pay would continue under all three assignments, but normal production overtime would not be available.
Employees assigned to the other plant would receive a company shuttle rather than mileage reimbursement.
Union steward Kori Bell said several employees rely on overtime for household bills; the union has requested a temporary income supplement.
The company has not agreed to the supplement and has not reported how many employees accepted their assignments.
Plant manager Ansel Pike said the new furnace should allow smaller bottle runs, which the current equipment handles inefficiently.
The company has not released a calculation of the new furnace's energy cost per bottle or its emissions.
Dunmere Power Cooperative has approved an electrical connection, but a required substation transformer is still on order.
The cooperative says the transformer must arrive by December for the announced installation schedule to hold.
Bell said, "Keeping a job and keeping the same paycheck are not quite the same promise."
Brindle is building bottle inventory for its 23 beverage-company customers and has offered them earlier delivery dates.
Customer Leda Marr, owner of Thistle Run Cider, said, "An early delivery helps only if I can find somewhere to put it."
Marr's business has rented a storage unit for the shutdown period; she would not disclose the rental cost.
The existing furnace began operating in 2004 and has undergone two scheduled rebuilds.
The grant requires annual employment reports for three years, but it does not guarantee unchanged overtime or a particular emissions reduction.

forbidden_additions: A guaranteed installation date despite the outstanding transformer
A quantified emissions reduction or unchanged total earnings for every worker
